english: In the Mahābhārata, the person who eats at the end of a fortnight has been called "one who lives by pickings and gleanings which means that, under such circumstances, the Householder has become the Hermit" But even so, this would be incompatible with the character of "one who does not possess enough for the morrow;" as, under the circumstances mentioned, the man would be "one who lives upon whatever he obtains," and not " one who does not possess enough for the morrow" That man is called "one who does not possess enough for the morrow," who earns everyday just enough for the day, and spends it all on the same day, and does not keep anything for the next day.
